draft.title: First Nations Australians' classification systems
card: First Nations Australians have observed and classified plants and animals for tens of thousands of years. This knowledge is passed on through stories, songs, art and practice.
Groups of First Nations Australians may sort living things by features such as use (food, medicine or tools), habitat, season and relationships.
Season is one example. Some plants and animals are grouped by the time of year they flower, fruit or are ready to be gathered, and the seasons used can differ from the four European ones.
The Linnaean system mainly groups living things by shared physical features. First Nations systems can group living things in different ways, and each system suits its own purpose.
draft.remember: First Nations Australians may classify living things by use, habitat, season and relationships, so groups can differ from Linnaean ones.

a.q: Which of these is a way First Nations Australians may group living things?
opts: By the season when a plant fruits or an animal is gathered
By the two-part Latin name used by scientists worldwide
By sorting each one into a rank such as order or family
By body features alone, the same way in every system
a.why: Many First Nations systems use features such as season, use, habitat and relationships. The other options describe the Linnaean system or say that body features alone are used, and the card shows that is not how these systems must work.
a.clue: Think about features linked to the land and the year.

b.q: A community groups a plant with a shellfish because both are gathered in the same season from the same coastal place. Why might this differ from the Linnaean system?
opts: It groups by habitat and season, not mainly by body features
It groups by Latin names, not by the places they are found
It uses only one feature, so it cannot be a proper system
It groups by physical features first, then by where they live
b.why: The groups here come from habitat and season, so a plant and a shellfish can sit together. The Linnaean system mainly uses shared physical features, which would place them in different groups. Different does not mean wrong, as each system suits its own purpose.
b.clue: Look at what the plant and shellfish share in this case.

proposal.title: First Nations Australians' classification systems
card: First Nations Australians have observed and classified plants and animals for tens of thousands of years. This knowledge is passed on through stories, songs, art and practice.

Groups of First Nations Australians may sort living things by features such as use (food, medicine or tools), habitat (where it lives), season and relationships (links between living things, land and people).
Season is one example. Some plants and animals are grouped by the time of year they flower, fruit or are ready to be gathered, and the seasons used can differ from the four European ones.
The Linnaean system mainly groups living things by shared physical features. First Nations systems can group living things in different ways, and each system suits its own purpose.
proposal.remember: First Nations Australians may classify living things by use, habitat, season and relationships, so groups can differ from Linnaean ones.

a.q: A community puts several plants in one group because each can treat a cough or heal a cut. Which feature is this grouping based on?
opts: Their use
Their habitat
Their season
Their relationships
a.why: Treating a cough or healing a cut is a medicine use, so the plants are grouped by use. Habitat would mean grouping by where the plants live, which the case does not mention. The card shows these systems can group living things in several ways, and this one is by use.
a.clue: Think about what people do with these plants.

b.q: A community groups a plant with a shellfish because both are collected on one beach when a certain tree flowers. Why might this differ from the Linnaean system?
opts: It links them by time and place, not by body features
It links them by body features, not by time and place
It links them by use as medicine, not by body features
It links them by one feature, so it is not a real system
b.why: The tree flowering marks a season, and the beach is a habitat, so the group is based on time and place. The Linnaean system mainly uses shared physical features, which would put a plant and a shellfish in different groups. Different does not mean wrong, as each system suits its own purpose.
b.clue: What do the tree flowering and the beach tell you?
